title: Tiered routing engine: quota-aware prioritization for free/paid/enterprise
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a quota-aware tier-based routing layer that prioritizes requests across free, paid, and enterprise tiers. The routing layer must honor per-customer and per-tier quotas, degrade gracefully by falling back to cheaper or quantized model variants when capacity is constrained, and expose deterministic priority circuits for canarying and A/B tests. This ticket covers design, prototype, and initial rollout to the staging region.
acceptance_criteria: Routing honors per-customer and per-tier quotas with configurable eviction/backpressure policy
Requests are classified into free/paid/enterprise with documented precedence rules
Quota-aware prioritization reduces tail latency violations for enterprise customers under load
Fallback model variant selection triggers within 200ms when target model capacity unavailable
End-to-end e2e tests and integration tests exist and pass in CI
Telemetry exposes priority/queue-length/evictions and shows expected behavior in fault inject scenarios
plan: Design API extension to include 'tier' and 'quota_token' fields on incoming requests
Implement in-memory priority queue on each serving node with global token leaky-bucket coordination for strict quotas
Add fallback selector that maps primary model -> compatible lower-cost variant (quantized/shorter-seq/cheaper-region)
Integrate with smart-routing policy engine for region and tier preferences
Expose admin controls in Console for adjusting tier weights and emergency overrides
Create canary rollout: 5% traffic in staging, then 10% in us-west, observe SLOs for 48h
notes: 2026-02-25: Architecture review - agreed to use per-node PQ with periodic global quota reconciliation (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/492)
2026-03-02: Prototype benchmarks on A100x1 show 3% added CPU overhead, queueing latency median +3ms under synthetic load (dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tier-routing)
2026-03-05: Security reviewed for quota token handling; KMS encrypt at rest required (ticket ENG-8302)
2026-03-09: Backpressure policy updated to prefer 'graceful-fallback' (quantized model) instead of outright rejection for paid tier; product approved
tests: Unit: quota token verification and token bucket refills
Integration: simulated multi-tenant load test across tiers with expected eviction counts
E2E: canary flow with fallback activation and rollback on >1% enterprise error rate
Chaos: kill model worker and validate fallback model served within 200ms
Performance: measure added tail latency at p95/p99 under spike
rollout_strategy: Phase 1: Staging canary (5%) – validate telemetry and correctness
Phase 2: Regional pilot in us-west (10%) with auto-rollbacks on SLO breach
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with console feature flags for tuning
Phase 4: Global rollout with enterprise-only hard quotas enforced
